one_line_contribution: That a success-only write filter turns staleness into a closed loop after a hidden rule change - stale retrievals suppress the very successes that would refresh the store - and that this loop produces persistent lock-in in an append-only retrieval bank but not in a continual QLoRA fed by the same filter, with a measurable exogenous-refresh dose needed to break it in each substrate.
closest_prior_work: Verified: 'Honest Lying: Understanding Memory Confabulation in Reflexive Agents' (arXiv:2605.29463, verified via s2cli paper, S2 channel) already shows self-written memory reinforcing false beliefs on ALFWorld, with a repetition-rate metric and 3/16 frozen environments solved after the fix - i.e. self-generated store content that persists and blocks correction, in the proposal's own environment. It does not kill the proposal: its memory is reflection text, there is no rule change, no write-starvation coupling, and no parametric arm. The closest threat on the shift side is 'Closing the Feedback Loop: From Experience Extraction to Insight Governance in Verbal Reinforcement Learning' (arXiv:2606.17591, verified, HF channel), which names exactly the retention-forgetting dilemma in non-stationary environments - retained stale insights cause negative transfer, discarding them causes forgetting - and governs it. That is the read-side half of the claim, already published, without the write-side coupling or the substrate contrast. Also verified and adjacent: Live-Evo (2602.02369, S2), EDV self-confirmation trap (2606.24428), Zombie Agents (2602.15654), Set-shifting Behavioral Test for Harnessed Agents (2607.13396, S2 - hidden reliability shift with paired no-shift control, the protocol this proposal manufactures by hand). What survives as new is the coupling framing plus the bank-vs-LoRA contrast and the escape-dose estimand; no verified paper does that pair.
strongest_objection: The headline pair is an update-rule artifact and is arithmetically pre-determined by Gate 0, not discovered by E1. The proposal contrasts an append-only unbounded bank (which by construction cannot forget, and whose top-3 stale share is a deterministic function of s_stale, the pre-shift store size and MiniLM similarity - all fixed at E0, which the proposal itself computes and pre-registers as 'the lock-in prediction') against a continual QLoRA whose gradient steps are, by construction, entirely on the most recent chunk. 'Context locks in, weights recover' therefore restates 'append-only has no recency weighting, chunked SGD is all recency'. This is the exact objection that sank opposite_sided_failure_under_shift in Appendix B, and the brief's rule 'No prediction entailed by a definition' is aimed at it. The informative pairs are FIFO-vs-continual and unbounded-vs-replay, and both are demoted to ablations; P1 and P3 are displacement arithmetic; the bank half of P4 (4 injected items at 1 % cannot dent a 150-item store) is arithmetic too. A skeptical AC will say the study confirms a computation it already did, and that the one genuinely open question - whether the agent's own post-shift exploration produces enough successes to escape - is a single scalar (s_stale, measured at E0) dressed as a dynamical claim.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Promote FIFO-N=150-vs-continual-QLoRA and unbounded-vs-replay-QLoRA to the headline contrasts, matched on effective recency, and report the unbounded-vs-continual pair only as the definitional bracket. (2) Make the estimand the residual: compute the lock-in trajectory that E0 arithmetic predicts, and report the *deviation* of the observed store composition and success curve from it - the loop is a finding only if the coupling makes recovery slower than the open-loop displacement count predicts, which is the one number no arithmetic gives you. (3) Add the write-everything self-collected bank (see missing_baseline) so the success filter is isolated without swapping the writer. (4) Replace the two-rung dose ladder with a continuous one (0.5/1/2/5/10/20 %) on fewer arms and more seeds; with two rungs and 3 seeds, 'the bank needs >= 10 %, the LoRA escapes at 1 %' is an order-of-magnitude assertion, not an estimate. (5) Add the reset-LoRA arm the brief's own binding objections demand. (6) Re-cost E3: as written it exceeds the stated total episode budget by itself.
missing_baseline: A self-collected write-everything bank - the same agent writing both successes and labeled failures (or all trajectories with outcome tags) - which is the only arm that removes the success filter while holding the writer's competence fixed. E4's expert-writer control changes the filter and the item quality at the same time, so 'the loop disappears with an exogenous writer' is confounded: expert post-shift items would also break a bank that had no success filter at all. Secondarily, the brief's own Appendix-B fix list demands a reset-LoRA arm, and the plan has only continual and replay QLoRA; and a recency/time-weighted retrieval bank (the cheapest read-side remedy any reviewer would ask about) is absent - the failure-decayed bank keys on feedback, not write time.

Judgment on the check itself: three queries with IDs and an honest note that WebSearch was unavailable is above average for this round, but all three queries interrogate the in-context/self-evolving-memory side and none touches the parametric side, which is half the claim - a search on self-training-on-own-successes under shift was never run. It also omits 2606.17591 (the published non-stationary retention-forgetting governance paper, the nearest read-side threat), 2605.29463 (self-reinforcing self-written memory on ALFWorld), 2608.00017 and 2605.05583, and it silently drops 2607.13396 even though the hidden-shift benchmark appears in the novelty card handed to the author. An empty return on a question never asked is not evidence of novelty, and here the unasked question is the substrate the proposal claims escapes.
